jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Integration of High-Temperature Heat Pumps in Industrial Processes - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
Do you want your research to help industry decide how to electrify its heat supply? At DTU Construct you will combine thermodynamics, optimisation and machine learning to build tools that make the business case for industrial high-temperature heat pumps clear, fast and reliable.

We invite applications for a fully funded PhD position in the Thermal Energy Section of the Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark. The position is part of HeatMinds, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by Horizon Europe. HeatMinds brings together 6 universities and research institutes and 12 industrial and research partners across Europe to develop industrial high-temperature heat pumps that upgrade low-grade waste heat to up to about 250 °C.

Your project will address decision making support for heat pump end-users from a first viability check to integration with the process, to flexible operation. You will demonstrate the findings in industrial use cases together with our partners.

Supervision: Prof. Ahmad Arabkoohsar and Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall goal will be, through adequate methodological advancements, to cuts the time and effort needed to assess where and how high-temperature heat pumps should be integrated into industrial sites, and what is their economic value. Your main task will be:

• Develop models to rapidly estimate performance and break-even point for specific sites
• Extent methods for heat pump integration that co-optimize heat recovery, electrification and flexibility provided by heat pumps
• Refine and validate methods during industrial secondments 
• Publish in international journals, present at conferences and take part in HeatMinds network training, summer schools and outreach.
 
You have:

• A solid background in engineering thermodynamics, heat transfer and energy technologies, e.g. conversion or storage systems 
• Familiarity with modelling and numerical simulations, for example for MSc thesis or student projects 
• Programming skills, preferably in Python, Matlab, Modelica or similar 
• Excellent written and spoken English, and the motivation to work in an international, goal-oriented environment.
 
MSCA eligibility: at the time of recruitment, you must not already hold a doctoral degree. You must also not have resided or carried out your main activities (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before your recruitment date.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The PhD salary will be based on the Marie S. Curie compensation scheme conditions and according to the grant agreement. Based on seniority the candidate will receive a minimum of DKK 30.264,08 (base salary) and DKK 1580,90 (PhD supplement). In addition, DTU will also pay pension consisting of 18,07%. Finally, it is possible to apply for family allowance. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. Starting date is anticipated as 1 April 2027 or according to mutual agreement. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Professor Ahmad Arabkoohsar ahmar@dtu.dk and Professor Adriano Sciacovelli adrsc@dtu.dk.

You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 24 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A copy of thesis (if available) or other publications (if available)
• A short critical literature review (max. 3 pages) on integration of high-temperature heat in industrial processes: select up to 5 relevant publications and explain your choice, compare their methods & findings, identify possible open research questions, explaining how your background would help you address them. Include at least one figure or table of your own making. 
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. We undertake research, education, innovation, and scientific advice of the highest quality within building design and processes, building construction and safety, building energy and technical services, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, coastal and maritime engineering, materials technology, manufacturing engineering, engineering systems design, design for sustainability, and thermal energy.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Are you our new Business Controller?
jobs.description:
Do you understand the story behind the numbers - and can you help the business act on it?

We are looking for an experienced Business Controller who can connect financial performance with the operational and commercial developments behind it. You will take ownership of key reporting, budgeting and forecasting processes, work closely with leaders across the organisation and turn financial results into clear insights, priorities and actions.

The department “Analytics & Modelling” works across Momentum Energy Group and provides reporting, performance analyses and financial decision support to business units, senior management and the Board. You will join a small team of 3 with broad exposure across the organisation and play an important role in strengthening how Momentum understands, forecasts and manages its financial performance.

Momentum Energy Group develops, invests in, owns and operates renewable energy assets across Denmark, Germany and Sweden. We are one of Denmark's largest owners of onshore wind turbines, with activities spanning the full lifecycle of renewable energy projects and a development pipeline comprising wind, solar PV and hybrid projects through a clear growth agenda.

What are your tasks?

As a Business Controller, you will contribute to, deliver, and coordinate central parts of Momentum's performance management cycle. You will work closely with business unit leaders and Group Finance to understand developments in revenue, costs, and profitability while ensuring these drivers are reflected accurately in our reporting and outlook. You will be a trusted financial partner who combines a deep financial understanding with a strong and curious commercial perspective.

Your responsibilities will include:

• As part of a team delivering the monthly management reporting, including timeline management, inputs, quality assurance and financial commentary based on consolidated accounts received from Group Finance.

• Analysing monthly performance against budget, forecast and prior periods and explaining the underlying revenue, cost, and profitability drivers.

• Working closely with business unit leaders to understand operational and commercial developments and translate them into financial implications.

• Participating in budgeting and forecasting processes for relevant business areas, including assumptions, risks, opportunities and scenario analysis.

• Following up on budgets and forecasts with the business and ensuring that deviations, risks and required actions are identified and addressed.

• Developing and maintaining relevant financial and operational KPIs that provide transparency into business performance.

• Preparing business cases, profitability analyses and ad hoc decision support for commercial and operational initiatives.

Who are you?

You are an experienced and commercially minded finance professional who wants to understand and communicate how the business operates. You build strong working relationships across functions, but you are also comfortable challenging assumptions and conclusions constructively. You can move seamlessly between detailed financial analysis and discussions with senior stakeholders, translating complex findings into clear, actionable insights.

You are motivated by working in a developing organisation where the role will evolve over time, creating opportunities to take ownership of new tasks and areas of responsibility as the business matures.

Qualifications

• At least 5-7 years of relevant experience within business controlling, FP&A, performance management or a similar finance role.

• A relevant degree within finance, economics, accounting, business administration or a related field.

• Strong experience with management reporting, budgeting, forecasting and variance analysis.

• A solid understanding of financial statements and the interaction between operational performance, profitability, cash flow and the balance sheet.

• Strong analytical and financial skills, including proficiency in Excel.

• Experience preparing concise management presentations and communicating financial insights clearly to financial and non-financial stakeholders.

• A proactive and independent approach, combined with strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills.

• Professional proficiency in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

What we offer

You will join a small and ambitious team with broad exposure across Momentum and direct interaction with business unit leaders and senior management. We prioritise professional development, personal balance and an inclusive workplace.

You will work at new our office in Roskilde together with 70 colleagues. Benefits include health insurance and a healthy lunch and fruit scheme.

Do you want to be a part of the journey?

If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, please apply as soon as possible, and no later than November 17, 2026, as we will be reviewing candidates on a rolling basis.

For questions about the role, please contact Head of Analytics & Modelling, Karoline Nylander at kny@momentumgreenenergy.com.

At Momentum, we believe that diversity strengthens our team. We therefore encourage everyone—regardless of gender, age, background, or culture—to apply for this position.

jobs.description:
Research assistant in IoT data, AI and digital twin technology
Are you interested in turning IoT data into intelligent digital twins of real-world systems? The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Aarhus University invites applications for a 6-month research assistant position in the Robots4Green project, working at the intersection of IoT data, artificial intelligence and digital twin technology. The position is based in Aarhus, Denmark, and starts on 1 January or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 6-month position from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
We are seeking a motivated research assistant with a strong background in data science and machine learning to contribute to research on AI for IoT data and digital twin technology. You will work with sensor data and develop the models that allow digital twins to monitor, understand and predict the behaviour of physical systems.

Your tasks will include:

• Applying signal processing and feature extraction methods to sensor time series, for example wind and environmental data
• Designing, training and evaluating machine learning models for forecasting and anomaly detection, with an emphasis on interpretable and reliable models
• Contributing to data pipelines and to the integration of models into a digital twin platform together with the project team
• Supporting experiments and demonstrations together with project partners
• Documenting results and contributing to scientific publications and project deliverables

The position may also include assisting in supervision activities at the department.

Prior experience with IoT or digital twins is an advantage. You will gain hands on experience with IoT data and digital twin technology while working closely with researchers in the Networks and Analytics research group and with academic and industrial partners in the project. The position is an excellent stepping stone towards a PhD or a career in industry.

Your profile
Applicants should hold a Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science or a similar field.

We are looking for candidates with:

• Solid programming skills in Python for data analysis and modelling
• Experience with machine learning frameworks such as scikit-learn and PyTorch or similar AI frameworks
• A strong foundation in statistics, probability and signal processing
• A good understanding of time series analysis
The following qualifications are considered advantages:

• Experience with graph-based machine learning, such as graph neural networks, or graph signal processing
• Knowledge of IoT systems, sensor data or data platforms
• Familiarity with digital twin concepts and simulation
• Experience from research projects, including interdisciplinary collaborations
• Teaching or supervision experience

Personal skills
We value good communication skills in English, the ability to work independently as well as in an international team, curiosity and a proactive, structured approach to problem solving.

Who we are
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at Aarhus University is a leading research institution with strong expertise in computer science, electrical engineering and wireless communication systems. We maintain active collaborations with industry partners and are involved in multiple national and international research projects on IoT, AI and digital twins.

You will be joining the Networks and Analytics (NAN) research group, which focuses on research and innovation in developing and applying internet technology across a wide selection of fields in electrical and computer engineering for real-world, large-scale applications. The NAN group has strong expertise in wireless networks, IoT, network security, data analytics, AI and cooperative multi agent systems, with extensive experience in smart energy grids, smart and integrated transport and satellite communication systems.

Our research group provides a dynamic and supportive environment where interdisciplinary collaboration is encouraged, and where you will work with both academic researchers and industry professionals on projects with real world impact.

Department website: https://ece.au.dk

What we offer
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering offers:

• An exciting opportunity to work on applied research in IoT data, AI and digital twin technology
• A well developed research infrastructure with access to laboratories, IoT equipment and computing facilities
• Close collaboration with industrial partners and direct pathways to real world validation
• An interdisciplinary and international research environment
• Opportunities to co-author scientific publications and build a foundation for a PhD
• A supportive work environment that values work-life balance, professional development and openness

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Helsingforsgade 10, 8200 Aarhus N (Denmark), and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Professor Rune Hylsberg Jacobsen, +45 41893252, rhj@ece.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 17 November 2026.

Application procedure
Short-listing is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Are you an experienced Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) professional with a passion for advancing evidence-based MHPSS practice in humanitarian settings? Danish Red Cross (DRC) is looking for a MHPSS Advisor to provide technical expertise, capacity development, and quality assurance to the Red Cross Red Crescent National Societies (RCRC) National Societies delivering community-based MHPSS interventions in humanitarian settings.

About the position and the assignments  

You will be based at the Danish Red Cross HQ in Copenhagen and will be part of the Health Team in the Technical Quality and Impact Unit of the International Department. The Health Team comprises technical advisors within health and mental health and psychosocial support. It ensures the availability of the necessary technical capacities to provide timely and relevant assistance and advice to DRC-supported operations, with a primary focus on the Africa, while also supporting MHPSS interventions in MENA, Europe and Asia regions as needed.

As a member of the Health Team, you will be working under the line management of the Health Team Lead and will also work closely with other colleagues at the DRC HQ and Regional and Country Offices (COs), as well as with NSs staff and volunteers. You will also collaborate with the colleagues from the International Federation of the Red Cross Red Crescent (IFRC) and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The position does not have programme management responsibilities but supports programmes through technical accompaniment, mentoring, and quality assurance.

Your main responsibilities will be to:

• Strategic planning and direction: Contribute to defining and rollout of DRC’s strategic directions within MHPSS in humanitarian settings. Support development and rollout of strategies, policies, and technical frameworks for MHPSS in humanitarian settings.
• Technical support and guidance: Provide evidence-based guidance and advice to DRC COs and National Societies on MHPSS priorities, approaches and activities, remotely or through country visits and missions to ensure that MHPSS interventions follow industry standards and good practice. Support development or adaptation and rollout of relevant technical tools and guidelines to meet operational needs.
• Strengthening of capacities: Support National Societies in assessing technical capacity needs, and in designing and implementing capacity-strengthening plans, including trainings, coaching, mentoring, and technical supervision.

Do you want to develop new methods for quantitative modelling of the shallow subsurface and geological processes? The Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland (GEUS) is looking for a researcher with a strong geological background and an interest in combining geoscientific observations, numerical modelling and scientific software development. 

  The position is a three-year, time-limited researcher position in the Department of Near Surface Land and Marine Geology (SURFACE) in Aarhus, expected to start on 1st of January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

  About the position 

  The position lies at the intersection of geology, geophysics, glaciology, numerical modelling and scientific software development. You will develop computational approaches that combine geological and geophysical observations with process-based and probabilistic models to create quantitative representations of the subsurface and glacial environments. 

  You will initially contribute to two ongoing research projects, ICESYNC and DREAM, while also taking part in research and development related to the national groundwater mapping programme and other activities at GEUS. 

  In ICESYNC, you will work with process-based modelling of erosion, sediment transport and deposition and investigate how modelled ice dynamics and sedimentary processes can be linked to geological and geomorphological observations. The work includes development of reproducible modelling workflows and pilot studies in Greenland and Denmark. 

  In DREAM, you will contribute to the development of a high-resolution probabilistic geological modelling framework based on drone-based TEM data. You will work with the integration of high-resolution resistivity models and their uncertainties with geological prior knowledge and other geoscientific data. The aim is to develop a semi-automatic, open-source workflow for constructing detailed geological voxel models and to test the approach using synthetic and field data. 

  Across these activities, you will work with numerical, probabilistic and process-based approaches to geological modelling and with integration of geophysical observations, geological data and process-based models. An important part of the position will be the development of reproducible computational workflows and scientific software for geoscientific analysis and modelling. You will also contribute to geological interpretation and modelling in research projects and applied activities, including the national groundwater mapping programme. 

  The position includes publication and communication of research through peer-reviewed papers, project deliverables, presentations and open-source software. You will also be expected to contribute to the development of new research ideas, project proposals and collaborations with Danish and international partners. 

  Who are you? 

  You hold a PhD, or have submitted your PhD before the application deadline, in geoscience, geophysics, computational geoscience or a closely related field. 

  We are looking for a researcher with a strong geological background and a good understanding of geological processes, combined with experience in quantitative geoscience. This may include numerical modelling, geological modelling, probabilistic or statistical methods, inverse problems, geostatistics or related approaches. 

  You should have a good understanding of geophysical data and their geological interpretation and strong programming skills, with experience in scientific software development, for example in Python, Matlab or a similar language. You should be able to work independently and systematically while contributing actively to an interdisciplinary research environment, and you should communicate well in written and spoken English. 

  Experience with TEM data, process-based modelling, 3D geological or voxel-based modelling, open-source scientific software or reproducible computational workflows would be valuable. Knowledge of Quaternary geology, glacial geology, sedimentology or groundwater geology would also be relevant, as would experience from externally funded research projects and preparation of research proposals. We do not expect applicants to cover all of these areas. 

  As Danish is the primary organisational language at GEUS, you should be prepared to learn Danish if you are not already a Danish speaker. 

  Meet your new colleagues 

  At GEUS, you will join the Department of Near Surface Land and Marine Geology, where we conduct research on a wide range of topics related to the processes, resources and geology of the upper 300 metres of the subsurface, both onshore and offshore. 

  Based at the university campus in Aarhus, the department consists of around 35 enthusiastic colleagues working in an interdisciplinary environment. We combine field observations, laboratory analyses, and advanced modelling to address scientific questions and societal challenges. 

  As part of the team, you will work alongside colleagues committed to scientific excellence, collaboration, and knowledge sharing. We work closely with public authorities, universities, and international research networks, providing a strong platform for developing your research, building collaborations, and making a meaningful contribution to both science and society. 

  A working environment with a focus on professional development and well-being 

  There are many good reasons why you should choose a working life at GEUS. 

  We are a diverse staff of about 300 committed employees. Trust and flexibility are keywords. The working environment is lively, informal and international. Our tasks are versatile and there are plenty of opportunities for you to influence the development of your task portfolio.

  We prioritise professional development, among other things by offering access to courses and other relevant activities. Socialising is also very important at GEUS, and we have a rich social life with a staff club, an art association and more. 

  At GEUS, we prioritise the well-being of every single employee. We prioritise that the Heads of Departments are close to the employees, and we have flexible working hours that allow you to organise your life so that there is time for what matters to you. If you need to work from home occasionally, that is also possible. 

  Furthermore, we have associated physiotherapists. 

  Salary and terms of employment 

  Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with the relevant trade union agreement. 

  The appointment area is the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities and its institutions. 

  The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities considers diversity to be an asset and encourages anyone regardless of gender, age, religion or ethnicity to seek the position. 

  Further information 

  If you would like additional information, please contact the contact Acting Head of Department Verner Brandbyge Ernstsen Verner vbe@geus.dk or Senior Researcher Anders Damsgaard on andam@geus.dk. 

  If you are an international applicant, you can read more about living and working in Denmark on GEUS’ website.  

  Are you interested? 

  If you are interested in the position, we would like to hear from you. The application must include a CV incl. your ORCID, a list of publications with a separate indication of articles registered in ISI Web of Science and any copies of individual publications of particular relevance to the position. Please enclose master's and PhD diplomas in either Danish or English as well as other material documenting qualifications at senior level. 

  Please apply for the position by clicking “Apply for position”. We must have your application at the latest on Sunday 15th of November 2026 (Danish time). 

  Applications or other material received after the deadline will not be considered. 

  The employment procedure 

  A professional assessment committee consisting of one internal and two external assessors at minimum senior researcher level will carry out an individual assessment of all applicants’ professional qualifications, and the applicants will be assessed as qualified or unqualified for the position. Afterwards, an internal employment committee will decide which of the professionally qualified candidates will be invited for a job interview. This procedure is in accordance with the “Order on employment and assessment of scientific staff at the Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland § 4 and 7”.
